title: Lesson 1: Your Personal Ministry
description: Four friends carried a man to Jesus, and Jesus saw their faith. This lesson opens Growing Out by showing that the love God poured into you keeps moving out, and that your personal ministry begins with the people already in your life.

courseLogo.alt: Growing Together Discipleship Series: Starting in Discipleship, Growing Out with the Gospel, and Leading in Discipleship
courseLogo.title: Welcome to Growing Out

blocks.text: The 200-level path has three connected courses. Growing Deep (201) was about loving God. Growing Up (202) was about loving the people God has placed beside you. Now in Growing Out (203), the branches begin to bear fruit, as that love reaches people who do not yet know Jesus.

blocks.title: Four Friends and a Roof
blocks.text:
Jesus was teaching in a house in Capernaum, and the crowd was so thick that no one else could get near the door. Then four men arrived, carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. He could not walk to Jesus, and now his friends could not carry him through the crowd.

They did not turn around and go home. They climbed onto the roof, dug an opening through it, and lowered the man down on his mat until he lay right in front of Jesus.

What happened next begins with a surprising phrase: "And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, 'Son, your sins are forgiven'" (Mark 2:5). Then, so everyone would know He has authority to forgive sins, Jesus told the man to get up. He stood, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. The whole crowd gave glory to God and said, "We never saw anything like this!" (Mark 2:12).

Notice that phrase: Jesus saw their faith. Mark does not give the four men's names, but they believed Jesus could help, and their faith went to work for a man who could not get there by himself. They could not heal him, and they could not forgive him. What they could do was carry him to the One who can.

Before you carry anyone, remember where you started. You were the one on the mat. You could not get to Jesus in your own strength, and someone carried you: a parent who prayed, a friend who invited you, a church that kept the door open. And Jesus did far more than meet you there. He carried your sin to the cross and said to you what He said to that man: your sins are forgiven. Carried people become carriers.

That is the heart of this course. God grows your faith so He can work through you for the faith of others. Your personal ministry is loving the people God has placed in your life and helping them know and follow Jesus.
1.1 - Who is one person you would love to see come to know Jesus?
Loved First, Then Sent

You have already walked most of this road. In Growing Deep, you saw the love that comes down: the Father who runs toward you, the Son who covers you, and the Spirit who guides you. In Growing Up, that love reached your neighbors, your family, and your church family. Growing Out is the same love, still moving, now reaching people who do not yet know Jesus. Step through the picture one more time and watch where it goes.

blocks.alt: Circles moving outward from You, loved by God, to Home, then Work and School, then Neighborhood, then The World, with arrows pointing out.

blocks.text: Love moves out the way this picture does. It starts with the people closest to you and keeps going. You do not start at the edge. You start at your own front door.

A fruit tree does not eat its own fruit. What God is growing in you is for someone else: your patience helps someone feel safe, your generosity lifts a burden, and your words help someone understand the good news.
1.2 - Who is being helped by what God is growing in you, or who could be?
Jesus Sends Ordinary People

After Jesus rose from the dead, eleven disciples met Him on a mountain in Galilee. Not long before, every one of them had run away, and even now, "when they saw him they worshiped him, but some doubted" (Matthew 28:17). Jesus did not go looking for a better team. He gave these forgiven, unsure, ordinary men His mission.

And Jesus came and said to them, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age."

This is called the Great Commission, and it is addressed to you too. Look at how it is wrapped. It opens with His authority and closes with His presence, and in between is one clear direction: go. Jesus does not tell His followers to wait and hope people come to them. He sends them. You do not have to be fearless or finished to be sent. You only have to belong to the One who sends you.
Love Has Names
So where do you go? Just before Jesus returned to the Father, He drew the same circles.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.

Jesus started His followers in Jerusalem, the city where they already were. The mission reaches the whole world, and you will come back to that later in this course, but it begins with the people who already know you.

The four friends did not carry a crowd. They carried one man. Loving your neighbor becomes real when your neighbor has a name and a face: the people in your home, the people beside you at work or school, and the people in your neighborhood and everywhere else you keep showing up. Love has names.

One question sits underneath every circle: Does everyone who knows me know the good news of Jesus? That is not asking whether you have preached at everyone. It is asking whether the people in your regular life have seen enough of your faith and heard enough of your story to know what you believe and why.
1.3 - Start your map here. Write two or three names for each circle: home, work and school, and your neighborhood.
A Life, Not a Project

Here is what personal ministry is not. It is not a program you sign up for, a class you pass, or a project you finish and check off. It is a lifestyle of love, lived on an ordinary Tuesday with the people already in your circles.

But a lifestyle still needs something to hold on to. Athletes have drills and musicians have scales. Followers of Jesus have rhythms they can practice until love for their neighbors becomes second nature. That is what the rest of this course gives you: BLESS, five simple rhythms for loving the names on your map.

blocks.title: The BLESS Rhythms
content: Begin with prayer. Talk to God about people before you talk to people about God.
Listen. Ask good questions and help someone feel known.
Eat. Open your table and share a meal.
Serve. Meet a need you have noticed, expecting nothing back.
Story. Share your story and the story of Jesus.

blocks.text: You Carry, Jesus Heals

If this feels like a lot, go back to the roof. The four friends did not heal anyone. Their part was to bring their friend close to Jesus, and what happened next was His part. It is the same for you. You cannot change anyone's heart, and God does not ask you to. He asks you to love people and bring them near. His Spirit lives in you to give you words and open doors, and the results belong to Him. Your part is to carry. His part is to heal.
1.4 - How would you explain your personal ministry to a friend in one minute?
This Week's Practice

Choose one name from your map, the person God is placing on your heart, and pray for them by name each day this week. It took four friends to carry one man, so tell one Christian friend the name you chose and ask them to pray with you.
Lesson 1 Review

Four friends carried a man to Jesus, and Jesus saw their faith. Before you ever carry anyone, you were the one on the mat, and Jesus carried you. Now the love that came down to you keeps moving out: to your home, your work and school, your neighborhood, and the ends of the earth. That is your personal ministry, loving the people God has placed in your life and helping them know and follow Jesus. It is not a project but a lifestyle of love, and BLESS gives you rhythms to practice it. You carry. Jesus heals.
In the next lesson, you will begin the BLESS rhythms where every one of them starts, with prayer for the names on your map.

What is one step you are going to take this week?
